s1.syndrome_frame: Persistent vertical misalignment with elevation deficit
salient_findings: Elevation deficit of the right eye
History of anomalous band in the right orbit
Presence of a right orbital linear soft-tissue lesion
key_facts: 52-year-old woman
History of long-standing diplopia
Previous MRI of the orbits revealed an anomalous band in the right orbit
Surgical excision of the anomalous band did not improve motility
Diplopia remained stable in primary gaze
Orthotropic in primary position
Elevation deficit of the right eye
MRI of the orbits showed a right orbital linear soft-tissue lesion
Lesion was medial to the medial rectus muscle and parallel to it
Lesion had enhancement and signal-intensity characteristics identical to those of extraocular muscle

shortlist.label: Brown syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Elevation deficit and previous anomalous band in the right orbit

shortlist.label: Thyroid ophthalmopathy
shortlist.why_kept: Orbital soft-tissue lesion with enhancement and signal-intensity characteristics identical to those of extraocular muscle

shortlist.label: Orbital myositis
shortlist.why_kept: Orbital soft-tissue lesion with enhancement and signal-intensity characteristics identical to those of extraocular muscle

shortlist.label: Idiopathic orbital inflammatory disease
shortlist.why_kept: Orbital soft-tissue lesion with enhancement and signal-intensity characteristics identical to those of extraocular muscle

shortlist.label: Superior oblique myokymia
shortlist.why_kept: Elevation deficit and previous history of diplopia

raw.rationale: The patient's history of long-standing diplopia, previous anomalous band in the right orbit, and current elevation deficit of the right eye, along with the MRI findings of a right orbital linear soft-tissue lesion medial to the medial rectus muscle, are consistent with Brown syndrome, which is characterized by a restrictive strabismus due to an anomalous or fibrotic superior oblique tendon or trochlea.

rejected.label: Thyroid ophthalmopathy
rejected.why: No measured proptosis or other signs of thyroid ophthalmopathy were noted

rejected.label: Orbital myositis
rejected.why: The lesion's enhancement and signal-intensity characteristics were identical to those of extraocular muscle, but there was no indication of inflammation or swelling of the extraocular muscles

rejected.label: Idiopathic orbital inflammatory disease
rejected.why: There was no evidence of inflammation or other signs of orbital inflammatory disease

rejected.label: Superior oblique myokymia
rejected.why: The patient's symptoms and MRI findings are not consistent with the intermittent, micro-tremor-like movements of the eye seen in superior oblique myokymia
